bindings.label: Female child aged 1 year 4 months presented with delayed psychomotor development and exotropia.

Admitted for evaluation of delayed psychomotor development and surgery for exotropia; born full term (40 weeks) via cesarean section after uneventful pregnancy; first child of healthy unrelated parents with no notable family history.
Upon admission, she exhibited a distinctive high-pitched cry and microcephaly (smaller than average head size).

Motor delays included delayed crawling, ability to sit without support but inability to stand; neurologic exam revealed hypotonia in the left leg, with normal tendon reflexes and cranial nerve function.
At 6 months of age, an echocardiogram identified a ventricular septal defect.
Genetic multisystem syndrome
Congenital infection syndrome
Perinatal brain injury
Laboratory testing shows 46,XX,del(p15.2)
Brain MRI shows brainstem hypoplasia, white-matter atrophy, thin corpus callosum, and reduced myelination
Chromosomal deletion syndrome at p15.2
Brain MRI additionally shows a large cisterna magna (mega cisterna magna)
CMA/WES, parental karyotype/FISH, and metabolic screening have not yet been performed
The chromosomal deletion is a de novo (sporadic, non-inherited) mutation
Cri-du-chat syndrome (5p deletion syndrome)
Chromosomal deletion syndrome at p15.2 (non-5p)
De novo chromosomal deletion syndrome with multisystem involvement
5p15.3 FISH/MLPA and high-resolution breakpoint mapping to confirm the Cri-du-chat critical region are recommended but not yet performed
Detailed echocardiographic VSD anatomy and cardiac ultrasound validation remain pending
Dysmorphology examination for minor anomalies remains to be completed
The 46,XX,del(p15.2) is a terminal 5p deletion involving the Cri-du-chat critical region at 5p15.3-p15.2
